validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION CONFIRMED, not a phantom or misclassified row. This is FERC Docket No. CP20-483-000, a real, completed loop-line expansion of El Paso Natural Gas Company's (EPNG, Kinder Morgan) existing 16-inch Line No. 3191 in Eddy County, New Mexico, plus minor compressor-station work at Eunice (Lea County, NM). Confirmed independently by (1) the Federal Register's own published notice of the docket filing (85 FR 39555, published by the Office of the Federal Register/National Archives, 2020-07-01) and (2) EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects database (Historical Projects tab, row dated 2020-05-04/2021-04-27). Both agree EXACTLY with the sheet's current values: 17.1 mi, 16 in, 159 MMcf/d, $23.5 million, completed/in-service 2021 (EIA states the precise date: 2021-02-28). A third document -- EPNG's own FERC Weekly Environmental Inspector Report No. 20 (filed 2021-01-14, covering 2021-01-04/01-10 construction activity in Eddy and Lea Counties, NM) -- corroborates the same specs and shows the project nearing completion on schedule in January 2021, consistent with the EIA completion date five weeks later. Correctly classified: an interstate FERC Section 7/blanket-certificate transmission-pipeline loop-line expansion, not a gathering/distribution line -- no classification concern. No duplicate: checked against all 46 roster rows: nothing else in the roster matches this length/diameter/capacity/cost combination or FERC docket. CAVEAT -- EIA's own 'Beg_State/End_State' columns code this project as NM->TX with 'Crosses State Border = Yes', but that is EIA restating the DOWNSTREAM delivery description ('takeaway capacity ... to the Pecos, Texas compressor station, and into Keystone pool') rather than this loop's actual construction footprint: both the Federal Register notice and EPNG's own weekly environmental report state plainly that ALL of the physical work (the 17.1-mile loop AND the compressor-station modifications) sits in Eddy and Lea Counties, New Mexico -- no Texas construction is described anywhere in either primary document. GEM's EndState/Province='New Mexico' (not Texas) is therefore CORRECT as recorded -- flagging this so nobody 'fixes' EndState/Province to Texas off the EIA table's Beg/End coding, which is the wrong axis to trust here. Opened 6 of the 12 harvested wiki citations directly (Wikipedia via the cite-1 bit.ly, which resolves to https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Paso_Natural_Gas; kindermorgan.com/Operations/Natural-Gas/Index; the now-dead kindermorgan.com/business/gas_pipelines/west/EPNG_MP/ project page, which redirects to the generic Index -- confirmed via curl, not usable standalone; the EIA data.php citation, chased to the actual downloadable EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjects.xlsx; and the EPNG weekly environmental report PDF, both live and Wayback-archived). Not pursued: the FERC three-digit pipeline code list (2013 archive, not project-specific), the Oct-2018 Pipeline News planned-projects PDF, and the two Pipeline Safety Trust / NTSB items (a 2000 Carlsbad pipeline rupture, a different, much earlier incident) -- all low-relevance by date/subject mismatch. The Reuters/Natural Gas Intel Aug-Dec 2021 items describe a fatal blast on a DIFFERENT EPNG segment in Arizona, months after Carlsbad South's Feb-2021 completion -- unrelated to this row's data but see the Delay flag note below.

validity.recommendation: clear Delayed/DelayType (blank) unless a specific delay episode can be sourced -- no evidence supports a delay on this project
validity.researcher_notes: Delayed=yes / DelayType=inferred looks like a stale or misapplied flag with no supporting evidence. EPNG's own FERC weekly environmental report states plainly: 'At the conclusion of the notice period for the Carlsbad South Project on August 24, 2020, the project was deemed approved' (i.e., no protest was filed; the standard prior-notice review ran its normal course under EPNG's blanket certificate, Docket CP82-435). The project was filed June 19, 2020 (Federal Register, 85 FR 39555) and completed February 28, 2021 (EIA) -- roughly 8 months from filing to in-service, which is an unremarkable timeline for this fast-track 'prior notice' authorization process, not a delayed one. The weekly inspector reports (I read Report No. 20, Jan 2021) show routine restoration/cleanup work proceeding on schedule, with one minor, promptly-corrected environmental housekeeping issue (secondary containment cleanup) -- nothing rising to a reportable delay. I did find independent coverage of a serious, UNRELATED event -- a fatal explosion on the broader El Paso Natural Gas mainline in Arizona in August 2021 (Natural Gas Intel, Reuters) that shut a different segment for months -- but that postdates Carlsbad South's completion by six months and is a different location/segment entirely; it should not be read as evidence of delay on THIS project. Recommend clearing the Delayed/DelayType flag on this row unless a researcher can point to a specific, sourced delay episode for Carlsbad South itself (I searched and found none).

validity.recommendation: correct EndLocation -- it is currently a misspelled duplicate of StartLocation ('Carslbad'), not a distinct, sourced endpoint
validity.researcher_notes: The Location cluster's own 'irregular' flag is earned: EndLocation reads 'Carslbad' -- a misspelling of, and identical in substance to, StartLocation 'Carlsbad'. Both primary sources I found (the Federal Register notice and EPNG's own weekly environmental report) describe the project as a single 17.1-mile LOOP LINE running through Eddy County, New Mexico, plus separate 'minor appurtenant facility modifications' at a compressor station in Lea County -- which the weekly report names specifically: 'Eunice Compressor Station Modifications' (Eunice, NM, is in Lea County, roughly 55 miles from Carlsbad). Neither document gives a milepost-to-place-name mapping for the loop's actual second terminus, so I cannot confirm the correct EndLocation value outright -- but I am confident the current value is wrong: a 'South' loop of an existing line does not begin and end at the same town, and the duplicate-plus-typo pattern reads like a placeholder rather than researched data. Eunice (Lea County) is a plausible lead for whoever picks this up next, given it is the only other place name the sources associate with this project, but I'm not staging it as a confirmed replacement since the compressor-station work may not mark the loop's physical endpoint. StartLocation='Carlsbad', StartState/Province='New Mexico', EndState/Province='New Mexico', and both CountryOrArea='United States' are all independently confirmed (see the REFS_ADDED fill) -- only EndLocation is in question.
